rooms.title: A contact center is not a phone system
rooms.blurb: A PBX connects extensions. A contact center adds queues, skills, lists, dispositions, and reports around those calls. Five9 Virtual Contact Center is that layer, hosted as a domain rather than as servers you rack.

rooms.title: The domain is the tenant
rooms.blurb: You sign into one domain. Skill groups, users, lists, prompts, scripts, and campaigns live there. Another domain does not inherit them.

rooms.title: Roles on the floor
rooms.blurb: The same person is not every role. Agents take contacts. Supervisors can sit in skill groups with agents. Administrators configure the domain. Reporting is its own permission: standard reports do not appear without the Reporting role and at

rooms.title: Three campaign types
rooms.blurb: Public admin topics describe three campaign types: inbound, outbound, and autodial. Inbound answers a DNIS and runs the campaign IVR. Outbound uses the dialer and an agent. Autodial also dials a list, and the planning topic groups it with i

rooms.title: Contacts, fields, and lists
rooms.blurb: A contact record is a row of fields. number1, number2, and number3 are the usual phone slots the dialer walks. Lists are sets of those rows attached to outbound and autodial campaigns.

rooms.title: Dispositions are the dialer's memory
rooms.blurb: A disposition is the outcome stored on a record. System dispositions and custom dispositions both exist. The disposition topic says many system dispositions are redialed five times if you leave the default redial count, and you can reset th

rooms.title: One profile, many campaigns
rooms.blurb: A campaign profile overrides campaign defaults such as the ANI. You may create many profiles. A campaign uses one profile at a time. The same profile can be on more than one campaign. You attach it in Advanced mode, and workflow rules can s

rooms.title: Two administrator applications
rooms.blurb: The technical requirements still describe a Java VCC Administrator and a web Administrator Console. Java is not supported on Mac workstations with ARM processors. On those machines the document says to use VCC Administrator via Web in Admin

rooms.title: User profiles before user accounts
rooms.blurb: The planning roadmap says to define user profiles before you add user accounts. A profile is the permission bundle. An account is the person. Creating people first and hoping the default permissions match the job is how reporting and call-v

rooms.title: Skill groups are the queues
rooms.blurb: Skill groups organize agent and supervisor users into the queues that belong to campaigns. A user can be in several groups. A campaign can list several groups.

rooms.title: Prompts before the script
rooms.blurb: The inbound and autodial roadmaps tell you to define and record prompts before you build the IVR. A Play or Menu module can only speak what the prompt library already holds, or what a text-to-speech entry supplies in that module.

rooms.title: Do-not-call is a list, and a module
rooms.blurb: Outbound product material lists DNC list management with time-zone rules and Certified Caller as compliance tools. Inside the IVR, Set DNC is a real module in the modules chapter. A spoken 'remove me' path should hit that module, not a note

rooms.title: Workstations that drop live calls
rooms.blurb: The technical requirements tell you to turn off Windows 11 Efficiency Mode on PCs that take live calls. Efficiency Mode can limit CPU and sleep inactive tabs, and the PDF says that can drop active Five9 calls. If you leave it on, use a high

rooms.title: Reason codes, voicemail, and what admin is not
rooms.blurb: Not every silence is a carrier failure. Agents have Not Ready states. TCPA manual touch even forces Not Ready when preview time expires. Skill groups can hold voicemail, greetings, and messages. Those are administrator objects with their ow

rooms.title: A DNIS answers only while the campaign runs
rooms.blurb: An inbound campaign receives calls for a DNIS and processes them with that campaign's IVR script. The inbound topic is blunt about state: if the campaign is not running, callers hear a busy signal.

rooms.title: The script is the inbound product
rooms.blurb: Once the campaign answers, the IVR script is the product the caller meets. The inbound topic lists custom greetings, loops and branching, collecting information, using contact data, voicemail when the queue is long, forward to a third party

rooms.title: Queue treatment is a choice, not a hope
rooms.blurb: The inbound topic allows custom prompts and hold music, a message when agents are unavailable, voicemail, and a forward to a third party. Those are different exits. Hold music is not voicemail. A forward leaves your agents entirely.

rooms.title: Priority and service level
rooms.blurb: The inbound topic says you can prioritize inbound traffic. Skill Transfer has a Priority tab in the community write-up. Skill groups themselves have service-level settings in the basic admin topic.

rooms.title: Schedules, not a stopped campaign
rooms.blurb: The campaign admin tree includes IVR script schedules for autodial and inbound campaigns. The planning topic tells you to set the campaign IVR schedule after the script exists. A schedule swaps treatment by time. Stopping the campaign does

rooms.title: Pause before the next call
rooms.blurb: Skill Transfer has Pause Before Transfer, in seconds, on the General tab. The default is 0. A value above 0 waits that long after an agent is selected before the call is delivered, so a queue does not slap the next call down instantly.

rooms.title: Inbound design review
rooms.blurb: A review you can finish in one sitting: DNIS, running campaign, script, skill on the Outbound Skills tab, overflow module, schedule, and pause. Each one has a public page. None of them is a trunk setting.

rooms.title: A list is not a campaign
rooms.blurb: Outbound and autodial campaigns dial lists of contact records. The list has an order. The campaign has a run state and a dialing mode. Uploading a CSV does neither of those.

rooms.title: Profiles filter the list the agent sees
rooms.blurb: Campaign profiles filter and sort lists, control agent pop-ups, and manage disposition counts. They also override defaults such as the ANI. One campaign, one profile. Workflow rules can swap the profile.

rooms.title: List penetration and vertical dialing
rooms.blurb: List penetration is the default. The dialer tries the first phone on every record, then the next phone on a later pass. Vertical dialing stays with one contact and moves across that contact's numbers before it moves on.

rooms.title: Reset is a loaded gun
rooms.blurb: Reset list position sends the dialer back to the top. Reset Disposition clears selected outcomes so those rows can dial again. Both act on lists currently loaded. The disposition topic says to reset only codes you know are safe.

rooms.title: Time zone and call analysis are guarded defaults
rooms.blurb: The campaign admin tree includes time zone dialing options, and the default-settings topic says call analysis and voice detection level ship with vendor defaults. Changing defaults can raise a compliance warning. The same topic says US doma

rooms.title: Call analysis is not a guarantee
rooms.blurb: Call analysis and voice detection level are defaulted campaign fields. Product pages also list answering-machine detection and automatic voicemail as agent-efficiency tools. None of those pages give you a percent accuracy you can put in a c

rooms.title: Local caller ID is a profile choice
rooms.blurb: The outbound product page lists local caller ID as a business-efficiency tool, and campaign profiles are the documented place to override the default ANI. Showing a local number is a profile and number-plan problem, not a skill-group proble

rooms.title: Preview lets the agent read first
rooms.blurb: Preview delivers the contact and, on the product page, CRM history before the call is placed. It is the mode for conversations that need context. It does not overdial, so abandon from extra ringing lines is not the design.

rooms.title: Progressive keeps one call per free agent
rooms.blurb: The outbound product page says progressive dialing automatically dials one customer per available agent and is what centers use when they want to avoid dropped outbound calls. The dialer product page also says progressive is appropriate whe

rooms.title: Power dials a ratio you chose
rooms.blurb: The dialer page says power dials a user-configured number of calls per available agent and adjusts from abandon rates. It points that mode at a small group with a large list. The outbound page says the same shape: a small sales team and a l

rooms.title: Predictive fills idle time, and it can drop calls
rooms.blurb: The dialer page says predictive mode uses algorithms to predict agent availability and is suited to more than 10 active agents. The outbound page says it increases time spent talking to people instead of dialing. Both are marketing descript

rooms.title: TCPA manual touch is a typed number
rooms.blurb: TCPA manual touch exists only on domains enabled for it. The community article says those domains are generally for telemarketing to cell phones without express consent, and that no other dialing mode is available. Contacts are shown and no

rooms.title: The defaults are the compliance posture
rooms.blurb: For every dialing mode, the default-settings topic says options start at values Five9 recommends for FCC, FTC, and UK Ofcom telemarketing rules. If you change them you can see a warning. The example field is Max Abandoned Call Percentage.

rooms.title: Pick a mode in one page
rooms.blurb: Use the person's job, not the logo. Context before the call is preview. A promise of no dropped calls and a small team is progressive. A small team and a huge list, with eyes on abandon, is power. A large team whose idle time is the enemy i

rooms.title: Blended is a staffing plan
rooms.blurb: The outbound product page says outbound works with inbound digital channels and that blended behavior lets agents move between inbound and outbound as inbound rises and falls. It does not add a campaign type named Blended to the planning ro

rooms.title: Autodial is the IVR's outbound
rooms.blurb: Autodial is the third campaign type. The planning topic groups it with inbound when it tells you to record prompts and build IVR scripts. It still uses lists, like outbound. Think of it as the dialer reaching a person and then handing them

rooms.title: Priority and ratio are campaign settings
rooms.blurb: The campaign admin tree includes a topic for campaign priority and ratio settings. This lab has not quoted that topic's fields, so it will not invent the numbers. What is safe to say is that inbound priority, Skill Transfer priority, and an

rooms.title: Not Ready is a real state
rooms.blurb: Agents are not always available. TCPA manual touch forces Not Ready when preview time runs out, and it does not dial. A blend that assumes every login is a dialer resource will over-predict.

rooms.title: After-call work feeds the next dial
rooms.blurb: A disposition is what the dialer remembers. A final code stops the record. A retryable code brings it back after the redial rules. Wrap time, in the simulator, is the gap before the agent is free again. Five9's pause-before-transfer is a di

rooms.title: Digital and voice share the person
rooms.blurb: The outbound page says the dialer works with inbound digital engagement, and Agent Desktop Plus is the screen where voice, digital, and context are meant to meet. A blend that is only a voice story misses chat and email sitting on the same

rooms.title: A blend you can defend
rooms.blurb: A defensible blend is a paragraph: which campaigns run, which skills overlap, which mode each outbound book uses, who may be stolen, what Not Ready does to the count, and which abandon window the domain uses. Every noun in that paragraph is

rooms.title: The module list is the vocabulary
rooms.blurb: The IVR modules chapter names the blocks you may place. The list includes Play, Menu, Get Digits, Input, Voice Input, If/Else, Case, Set Variable, Lookup Contact Record, Query, Skill Transfer, IVA Transfer, Voicemail Transfer, Set DNC, Thir

rooms.title: Play, Menu, digits, and voice
rooms.blurb: Play speaks a prompt or TTS. Menu takes a choice and has an exit per option. Get Digits and Input collect what the caller types. Voice Input and the Natural Language Processing module are the speech-side blocks in the same chapter. Input is

rooms.title: If/Else is two ways. Case is more
rooms.blurb: If/Else has two branches. The modules chapter includes both If/Else and Case. When you need three or more outcomes, Case is the block that exists for that. Nesting If/Else until the drawing looks like a hedge is how scripts become unreviewa

rooms.title: Skill Transfer has more than a skill name
rooms.blurb: The community article lists General, Skills, Announcement, Priority, Connectors, Queue Callback, and Disposition. It also says 'six tabs' and then names more than six. Count the tabs in your editor. Do not trust the word six.

rooms.title: Variables, lookup, and query
rooms.blurb: Set Variable writes a value. Lookup Contact Record reads the contact. Query calls out, and the published example is an XML web service POST whose response groups are mapped with regular expressions into variables. That example uses script v

rooms.title: IVA, foreign scripts, DNC, and leaving the platform
rooms.blurb: IVA Transfer hands the call to a Studio task. Foreign Script jumps to another IVR script. Set DNC is the removal action. Third Party Transfer leaves your agents. Language switches prompt language. These are five different exits. A diagram t

rooms.title: Visual IVR and frames
rooms.blurb: The technical requirements say administrators can apply web page security so a Visual IVR script is not embedded in a frame where the user can be hijacked. The mechanism named is the X-Frame-Options header. The browser table in that PDF lis

rooms.title: A skill is a queue with people in it
rooms.blurb: A skill group holds users who have the agent or supervisor role. Campaigns point at one or more groups. The people, not the name, determine who can receive the contact.

rooms.title: The tab is named backwards on inbound
rooms.blurb: Outbound campaigns take skills on the Skills tab. Inbound and autodial take them on a tab named Outbound Skills. The skill topic says this in one paragraph. People miss it because the word outbound sits on an inbound campaign.

rooms.title: One module, one skill, when you need the truth
rooms.blurb: Skill Transfer may list several skills, and any agent who has one of them can take the call. The same article recommends a single skill in the module when you want reports that mean something.

rooms.title: Skill level versus list order
rooms.blurb: The skill transfer article describes an option to ignore the order of skills in the module and distribute by the agent's skill level instead. Order and level are different ideas. Order is the list you typed. Level is a property of the agent

rooms.title: Default is a queue, not a compliment
rooms.blurb: If Skill Transfer has no skill selected, the article says calls go to users who are not assigned skills. That queue is labeled Default in the softphone. It is a catch-all, not a place you want billing calls.

rooms.title: Service level is the scoreboard
rooms.blurb: The skill topic includes service levels. A service level answers 'how fast is acceptable,' usually as a percent of contacts answered inside a number of seconds. It does not, by itself, reorder the queue. Priority does the ordering. The scor

rooms.title: Skill voicemail is its own mailbox
rooms.blurb: The skill topic covers routing voicemail to the group, greetings, messages, and audio files. That mailbox is not the campaign Play prompt and not an agent's personal phone mailbox unless you have built it that way.

rooms.title: One screen is the product
rooms.blurb: Agent Desktop Plus is described as a single screen so the agent can stay with the customer. The Engage page adds real-time transcription, AI Agent Assist, and case context on that screen. The same underlying technology is what the desktop p

rooms.title: Plus adapters speak HTTPS and WSS
rooms.blurb: The technical requirements say Plus adapters use HTTPS and Secure WebSocket. If a proxy is in the path, it must support WSS. The PDF also says Five9 does not support TLS 1.1, and that browsers need TLS 1.2. Unencrypted API connections are r

rooms.title: Transcription and assist are features you turn on
rooms.blurb: The Engage page describes transcription, sentiment language, and Agent Assist suggestions on the desktop. GenAI Studio's page says it powers Five9 AI applications and initially focuses on Agent Assist summaries, with control over the output

rooms.title: WEM lives in the same desktop
rooms.blurb: The desktop page says Plus can show schedules, adherence, time-off requests, and evaluations without another app. CRM connectors can surface the same WFO actions inside Salesforce and the other named CRMs.

rooms.title: Digital text can be blocked
rooms.blurb: The technical requirements say some antivirus software, naming Avast as an example, can stop chat, social, or email text from loading. Voice can continue. The symptom is a blank digital pane, not a busy DNIS.

rooms.title: Headsets and the path under the desk
rooms.blurb: USB noise-canceling headsets are the recommendation. Analog is not supported. Wireless is discouraged above about ten active agents because of delay. Wired LAN is preferred. Wi-Fi is tolerated only when bandwidth holds. Satellite and cellul

rooms.title: The desktop review
rooms.blurb: A desktop review is short: one screen, WSS through the proxy, TLS 1.2, the schedule visible, text not blocked, USB headset, supported path, Efficiency Mode off, and the bandwidth rows added up. Each line is from the product page or the PDF.

rooms.title: Five9 WEM and a Verint path both exist
rooms.blurb: The workforce page says Five9 offers WEM natively and also partners with vendors such as Verint so a customer can fit the suite they already run. It says Five9 manages installation, configuration, maintenance, and upgrades for the WEM solut

rooms.title: Workforce management is the roster
rooms.blurb: WFM, in the product language, is how you staff to the work: schedules, intraday changes, adherence. It is not the dialer mode and not the service level target, though it exists so those can be met.

rooms.title: Quality management listens on purpose
rooms.blurb: The product page describes multi-channel evaluations, desktop monitoring, and automated scoring. The desktop page says agents can review evaluations without leaving Plus. That is QM: a sample of work, a score, a conversation with the person

rooms.title: Analytics and surveys sit beside the call
rooms.blurb: The data sheet and the product page put interaction analytics and customer surveys next to QM and WFM. Analytics is how you see topics across many calls. A survey is how the customer scores the one call. They are not the abandon rate and th

rooms.title: Recordings expire
rooms.blurb: The retention page says VCC audio recordings are kept for the sooner of 30 days or a successful SFTP or FTP offload, or as the contract says. E911 call recordings are listed at 30 days. Agent data is 60 days. Campaign state is 120 days. Dis

rooms.title: The agent should not need a second login
rooms.blurb: The desktop page's point is that schedules, adherence, time off, shift bidding, and evaluations are reachable in Plus and, through connectors, in the CRM. A second password for WEM is a design smell if the connector was in the contract.

rooms.title: What this lab will not pretend to run
rooms.blurb: This lab has no live WEM tenant. You cannot approve a real time-off request here. You can say which product page promised the button, which retention clock will delete the evidence, and which dialer mistake a bad roster causes.

rooms.title: Studio has regions
rooms.blurb: The technical requirements publish Studio portal hosts by region: five9.us, five9.au, five9.ca, five9.uk, and five9.br studioportal.io, plus older inferencecommunications.com names. A task built in the wrong region will not be the task your

rooms.title: A task key is not a vibe
rooms.blurb: IVA Transfer is a module. It needs a task to transfer to. The digital integration article, dated in the community as 26 March 2026, says you copy a ChatBot task key into the VCC IVA transfer side after the Studio task exists.

rooms.title: Contain, or hand back with context
rooms.blurb: A useful bot either finishes the job or returns the caller to a skill with the reason intact. IVA Transfer that dead-ends, or a Skill Transfer with no skill, is how you manufacture the Default queue.

rooms.title: GenAI Studio is a hub, not a slogan
rooms.blurb: The GenAI Studio page describes a low-code hub: choose among models, attach knowledge and customer data, test on real call data, keep a prompt library, and control output. It says the hub powers Five9 AI applications and initially focuses o

rooms.title: NLP in the IVR is not the same as Studio
rooms.blurb: The modules chapter includes a Natural Language Processing module and Voice Input, and it also includes IVA Transfer. They are different blocks. NLP inside a script is not automatically a Studio task, and a Studio task is not automatically

rooms.title: Prompts are a production change
rooms.blurb: A prompt library in GenAI Studio is production configuration. Changing a summary prompt changes what agents and customers are told. The page says you can test with call data and control output. A change without a test is how a policy you do

rooms.title: A bot review you can finish
rooms.blurb: Region, key permission, task type, failure branch, named skill, variable the agent sees, prompt test, and the recording clock. Eight checks. Each one has a page. A bot project that cannot pass them is a slide.

rooms.title: The adapter family
rooms.blurb: The technical requirements list Plus adapters for Agent Desktop Toolkit, Epic, Microsoft Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Oracle, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Zendesk. They use HTTPS and Secure WebSocket. The desktop page says a pre-built adapter and

rooms.title: Salesforce versions move
rooms.blurb: The technical requirements fetched for this lab say the Salesforce managed package is 2.46, SAML 2.0 is supported, and Lightning CTI is supported on Sales Cloud and Service Cloud for Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited, and Performance. Lig

rooms.title: ServiceNow releases are named
rooms.blurb: The same PDF says the ServiceNow Plus adapter supports the Service Operations and Configurable workspaces, and names the Australia, Zurich, and Yokohama releases. Those names are a support list with a date on it, like the Salesforce package

rooms.title: The rest of the named CRMs
rooms.blurb: Dynamics 365, Zendesk, Oracle, NetSuite, and Epic are in the same Plus adapter list as Salesforce and ServiceNow. The PDF does not give this lab a package number for each of them. Absence of a number here is not absence of an adapter.

rooms.title: SDK and connectors when there is no adapter
rooms.blurb: The API product page lists a CRM SDK and web connectors beside the CTI, configuration, reporting, and statistics web services, plus Web2Campaign. The desktop page says bring your own CRM with the SDK.

rooms.title: Screen pop down, voice up
rooms.blurb: This is the signature adapter incident. The caller is heard. The record is not on screen. Causes you can cite: WSS blocked, TLS 1.1, the wrong CRM chapter, an unassigned campaign profile that was supposed to control pop-up behavior, or a co

rooms.title: Salesforce modules inside the IVR
rooms.blurb: The IVR modules chapter includes a Salesforce module and an SFDC Einstein module, plus Contact Update and Lookup Contact Record. Those run in the script, before an agent exists. They are not the Plus adapter the agent uses after connect.

rooms.title: Three ways a call can enter
rooms.blurb: The technical requirements describe three SIP stories. Five9 can provide ITSP trunks. Your ITSP can connect to Five9 session border controllers, and there is a checklist for that. Or a gateway you already own — Avaya, Cisco, or Asterisk — c

rooms.title: DNS, codecs, and the default voice
rooms.blurb: The requirements prefer DNS SRV for the SIP targets. G.711 is the default codec, and the PDF describes it as uncompressed. Do not invent a packetization time. A 20 millisecond ptime shows up in practitioner notes about Cisco gateways. It is

rooms.title: How much bandwidth a seat costs
rooms.blurb: The requirements give planning numbers. Agent Desktop Plus and the Plus adapters are 128 kbps. The Java agent is 88 kbps. Agent Assist adds about 12 kbps. A VPN adds about 64. CRM or other business apps add about 64. A UC client such as Tea

rooms.title: NAT, idle timers, and split tunnels
rooms.blurb: NAT and PAT are acceptable. Double NAT is not. UDP bindings that idle out cause one-way audio. The requirements use a 30 second UDP idle timeout as the planning number, and they tell you to send keepalives when the binding is shorter.

rooms.title: Direct Connect and the edges
rooms.blurb: Direct Connect in the requirements is a Layer-3 handoff. There is no Layer-2 requirement. The port is 10, 100, or 1000 full duplex, and failover uses BGP. Equinix Fabric edges named in the PDF this lab read are Chicago CH3, Washington DC10,

rooms.title: TLS, and ports that are not universal
rooms.blurb: Unencrypted APIs are not the story. TLS 1.2 is required. TLS 1.1 is not supported. The requirements also list TLS 1.3 inbound ciphers: AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM, and CHACHA20.

rooms.title: Headsets, and the call that only fails one way
rooms.blurb: USB noise-canceling headsets are the recommendation. Analog headsets are not supported. Wireless is not recommended once you are above roughly ten agents. Windows 11 Efficiency Mode can drop live calls. Java admin is not the Mac ARM path; u

rooms.title: The API names on the product page
rooms.blurb: The APIs and SDKs page names CTI Web Services, Configuration Web Services, Reporting Web Services, Statistics Web Services, Web2Campaign, the CRM SDK, and Web Connectors. The same page also says REST. It does not, in the text this lab relie

rooms.title: Reporting is a role
rooms.blurb: Standard reports do not appear because you are an administrator. The community reporting article says you need the Reporting role and at least one reporting permission.

rooms.title: Layouts, and the matrix that will not export
rooms.blurb: The same reporting guidance describes three layouts: Tabular, Summary, and Matrix. A matrix answers a cross-tab question. It is not the layout you hand to a spreadsheet as a direct CSV.

rooms.title: The call log is a window, not an archive
rooms.blurb: The call log report is the place people look for one call. The community article on filters, dated 14 July 2026, describes a window of about 60 days unless retention has been extended.

rooms.title: Call variables are not history
rooms.blurb: Call variables can be reported when two things are true: the user has permission to edit them, and the variable is enabled for reporting. The community article is explicit that they are not historical. Turn the flag on today and yesterday's

rooms.title: Prebuilt UC and the connector that is not an adapter
rooms.blurb: The product material names prebuilt connections for Zoom Phone and Microsoft Teams. A prebuilt path is a product. A Web Connector that opens a URL is also a product. They are not the bandwidth line you add for a Teams client on the agent's

rooms.title: What an extract is allowed to remember
rooms.blurb: Reporting Web Services can move numbers out of the domain. Retention still applies to what Five9 keeps, not to the warehouse you built. Once a row is in your bucket, your policy owns it.

rooms.title: There is no import button
rooms.blurb: This track is a teaching bridge. Five9's public pages name Cisco as a SIP gateway type. They do not publish a wizard that reads a UCCX script or a UCCE dial plan and emits a domain.

rooms.title: CSQs, skills, and the partition you will not find
rooms.blurb: In this teaching map, a UCCX contact service queue is closest to a Five9 skill group: the people who can take that work. A UCCE skill group is a similar idea with a different name. Precision queues and attributes do not have a one-field equ

rooms.title: Scripts are rebuilt in modules
rooms.blurb: A UCCX script is a document in Cisco's editor. A Five9 IVR script is a chain of modules from the IVR Administrator's Guide: Menu, Get Digits, If/Else, Skill Transfer, Play, and the rest of that chapter. The lab's builder speaks those names

rooms.title: Dialing modes do not survive the move by osmosis
rooms.blurb: UCCE outbound has its own pacing words. Five9's product pages talk about Preview, Progressive, Power, Predictive, and Manual Touch. The simulator in this lab is a classroom clock, not either vendor's algorithm.

rooms.title: Numbers, lists, and ANI are a data project
rooms.blurb: DNIS values, calling lists, dispositions, and do-not-call entries are domain data. They are not inside the Cisco script file. A cutover that moves only the IVR still has nothing to dial and nowhere legal to send a call.

rooms.title: The gateway cut, without pretending to be the CUBE guide
rooms.blurb: When the third SIP story is a Cisco gateway, the technical requirements are still the Five9 side: DNS SRV preferred, G.711 as the default codec, TLS 1.2, no double NAT. What the gateway itself must rewrite — number format, a normalization s

rooms.title: Cutover morning is a checklist, not a mood
rooms.blurb: The morning the numbers move, the domain should already contain skills, a script, a running inbound campaign, loaded lists, dispositions, DNC, an assigned profile, and a desktop the agent has signed into. E911 addresses have to be dispatcha

rooms.title: 911 is a location, not a prefix
rooms.blurb: The E911 data sheet says agents dial 911 directly, with no prefix, and that the service sends a dispatchable location. It names the United States and its territories, Kari's Law, and RAY BAUM'S Act. The partner named on that sheet is RedSky

rooms.title: The address has to be the room they are in
rooms.blurb: A dispatchable location is the place responders can find a person. A headquarters address while the agent is at home is the failure the EULA describes. Remote and hybrid floors have to register the location the agent is actually using.

rooms.title: Recording is the customer's duty too
rooms.blurb: The EULA treats recordings as customer data. It says calls can be recorded while the caller is on hold and after a transfer. It puts notice and consent on the customer, who has to follow the laws that apply to their calls.

rooms.title: Retention is several clocks
rooms.blurb: The public retention page splits the clocks. VCC audio is the sooner of 30 days, a successful SFTP or FTP offload, or the contract. E911 recordings are 30 days. Agent data is 60 days. Campaign state is 120 days. A disabled domain is 120 day

rooms.title: Attestation is not an ANI field
rooms.blurb: Certified Caller is Five9's published STIR/SHAKEN program, tied to FCC and CRTC expectations. A campaign profile that overrides ANI changes what you present. It does not, by itself, mean the call is attested.

rooms.title: Abandon rate is a regulated posture
rooms.blurb: Default campaign settings call out a warning if you change Max Abandoned Call Percentage. Other fields on that page include Max Queue Time, Show Out of Numbers Alert, Monitor Abandoned Call Percentage, Call Analysis, Voice Detection level,

rooms.title: TCPA manual touch is a physical control
rooms.blurb: On domains where TCPA manual touch is enabled, other dialing modes are not available. Agents type the external number. Paste and drag are blocked. Dial enables only when the typed number matches. If preview times out, the agent goes Not Rea

rooms.title: The domain has neighbors
rooms.blurb: A Five9 domain does not live alone. Voice arrives on a SIP story. Agents sit in a desktop. WEM or a partner workforce suite watches the roster. A CRM pops. GenAI Studio may draft a summary. E911 carries a location. Reports leave through a r

rooms.title: Workforce, quality, and the recording shelf
rooms.blurb: The WEM product page describes workforce management, quality, analytics, surveys, and recording, and it also describes a Verint partnership. Five9 says it manages install and upgrades for the solution it delivers. The data sheet is the shor

rooms.title: Analytics and the report that is not a dashboard rumor
rooms.blurb: Analytics shows up on the WEM page and inside reporting. They are not one button. Standard reports need the Reporting role. Categories include ACD Queue, Campaign, Call Log, and the rest of that list. Layouts are tabular, summary, and matri

rooms.title: AI agents are a handoff with a name
rooms.blurb: Five9 Engage talks about self-service and the agent desktop together. Studio holds a digital IVA task. GenAI Studio is where knowledge and prompts are tested, and the product page says it powers Five9 AI applications, starting with Agent As

rooms.title: CRM, UC, and the desktop are three contracts
